spec_match.rationale: Covers the contract corners the other concepts do not: watchPosition with accuracyMode, options being fixed for the life of a watch (switch = clearWatch + restart), live permission state via the Permissions API change event, and the silently-dropped-member case surfaced with the getter probe at load.

interactive.rationale: Start/switch/stop buttons manage a real watch with correct disabled-state transitions, four live readout tiles, and a capped, timestamped event log that already receives real entries at load (permission state, capability verdict).

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises watch with a mode, mid-watch switching, live permission state and the failure branches including a silently-dropped accuracyMode — all present, and the last one was observed firing on this build.

edge_cases.rationale: This page is the edge-case concept and earns it: denied watches are proactively cleared with an explanatory log line ('a denied watch will never produce a fix'), all three error codes are named, missing geolocation and missing Permissions API both degrade with copy, and the log is capped at 40 entries.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite includes watchposition-callable and the permission-query assertion this page's readout depends on; on Chromium 141 the route ran 6 pass / 2 fail, the expected pre-157 split, and the page's own load-time capability line agreed with the failing getter-read assertion.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): load-time behaviour genuinely observed — console and the rendered log both showed 'accuracyMode is NOT read by this browser — both modes return a precise fix' and 'permission state: prompt', with the Permission tile reading 'prompt' in both screenshots; the watch lifecycle itself needs a permission grant and clicks, so it is judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert covers watch fixes (with accuracy, mode, count), watch errors by code and mode switches; console is clean apart from the page's own labelled lines.

design_system.rationale: All colours are variables; log state lines use --accent-blue (~7:1 on stone) and error lines --accent-rose (~4.8:1), both AA; buttons override background and color and disabled states are visually distinct.

accessibility.rationale: The event log is an aria-live=polite list with an aria-label, the readout is a definition list, the mode select is labelled, button disabled states communicate watch state, and the capability verdict is conveyed as text.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: controls wrap, readout tiles stack to one column, the log stays inside its scroll container, and there is no horizontal overflow or clipped control on either class.

openQuestions.title: Surface the not-implemented verdict next to the mode select, not only in the log
openQuestions.detail: On this pre-157 build the load-time getter probe correctly logs 'accuracyMode is NOT read by this browser', but the accuracyMode select and Start button still present the two modes as if they were meaningful; a user who does not read the log can run an 'approximate' watch and believe the fixes are coarse. Mirror the capability verdict as a small inline notice beside the select (or annotate the option labels) when the member is not read.

openQuestions.title: Fix lines credit the current select value rather than the running watch's mode
openQuestions.detail: onFix logs 'mode requested: ${mode.value}', reading the select at fix time. The select can be changed without pressing Switch (Switch also flips it programmatically), so a fix from a watch started as 'approximate' can be logged as 'precise' if the user merely moved the select. Capture the requested mode in begin() and close over it in the fix handler so the log states the mode the watch was actually created with.

summary: The edge-case concept the portfolio needs, and the strongest honest-degradation evidence in this feature: at load on this Chromium 141 build the page itself announced 'accuracyMode is NOT read by this browser — both modes return a precise fix' in its event log, alongside a live 'prompt' permission readout from the Permissions API. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/approximate-geolocation/watch-mode-switch/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots showing the populated log and tiles, clean console, feature /conformance/ route 6 pass / 2 fail as expected pre-157). The watch lifecycle needs a real grant and clicks, so it is judged from wiring, which looks correct including the deliberate clear-on-denial. Two small truthfulness upgrades: put the capability verdict next to the controls it invalidates, and log the mode a watch was started with rather than the select's current value.
